tone.voice: a knowledgeable doctor who speaks plainly — never condescending, always clear
tone.avoid: alarming, overly casual, jargon-heavy, cold or robotic

ux_norms: clarity above all — no ambiguous actions in a health context
large readable typography — accessibility is non-negotiable — minimum 16px body text
never use dark mode as default — light clinical environments build trust and aid readability
emergency contact or help is always accessible from any screen — never buried
privacy indicators always visible — lock icon, HIPAA badge, or data use note on screens handling sensitive data
progress indicators for all multi-step flows — booking, onboarding, form completion
patient app screens: home health dashboard leads with upcoming appointment — never with feed or discovery
patient app screens: prescriptions always show next dose time and refill remaining — never just a list
patient app screens: medical records use timeline view — chronological, most recent first
patient app screens: doctor profile shows credentials, years of experience, and patient rating before any other detail
patient app screens: telehealth waiting room shows estimated wait and doctor preparing status — never blank
patient app screens: consultation active screen has end call always red, always in the same position
notification and reminder system is prominent — medication reminders are mission-critical, not decorative
never show medical information in a way that could cause alarm without context — always pair data with normal range

visual_language.style: clean, friendly medical illustrations — not clinical or scary
photography_rules: real doctor photos for profiles — professional headshots only
diverse representation in all human imagery
patient photos only with clear consent context
visual_language.background_treatment: clean white or very light blue-grey — calm and clinical without being cold
visual_language.empty_state_style: friendly SVG illustration — stethoscope, clipboard, or health icon with reassuring copy
visual_language.onboarding_visual: clean friendly vector illustration — approachable health theme
visual_language.illustration_style: flat vector, soft rounded shapes — medical but not intimidating

compliance_notes: HIPAA compliance required in US market
data encryption and security must be communicated clearly

avoid: Never use dark mode as default — high contrast light UI is accessibility standard in healthcare
Never use red for branding, decorative elements, or non-urgent states — red means emergency
Never truncate medical information — dosage, instructions, and warnings always in full
Never use casual or colloquial language for medical information — precision is patient safety
Never show another patient's data — HIPAA compliance is absolute
Never gamify medication adherence with points or streaks — trivialises compliance
Never hide a crisis resource or emergency contact behind more than one tap
Never use dark patterns that obscure the cost of a medical service before commitment
enforce: Emergency contact and crisis resources always one tap away
HIPAA compliance badge visible on all data-sharing and messaging screens
All medical data changes logged with timestamp and user ID
Doctor credentials and verification badge always visible
Prescription expiry always shown with amber warning before expiry
Lab results always shown with reference range — never just the value
Medication interaction warnings always shown before prescription confirmation
Accessibility: minimum 16px font size for all medical information
